newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: BOND SENTENCED TODAY
There'll be a sequel this morning to what's described as Australia's biggest case of corporate fraud, when former tycoon Alan Bond is sentenced in Perth.
Bond is already serving a three year sentence for fraud offences relating to a French painting, La Promenade.
He's now facing the possibility of a further jail term for two offences of acting dishonestly as a company director.
These related to the transfer of hundreds of millions of dollars from the company, Bell Resources, to Bond Corporation in 1988 and 1989.
Both charges carry a maximum sentence of five years.
POLICE COMMISSIONER DENIES BREACHING CODE OF CONDUCT
The office of New South Wales Police Commissioner has denied that Peter Ryan has breached the Service's day-old code of conduct by accepting free theatre and football tickets.
A spokesman has confirmed that Mr Ryan paid his own way to the AFL grand final in Melbourne last year, but accepted free entry tickets.
He's also accepted tickets to Sydney theatre shows.
However, his office says any police officer may accept gifts of nominal value from another organisation as long as permission is sought from the officer's supervisor.
A register is also being kept of such gifts.
Mr Ryan's spokesman says any constable would be able to accept similar gifts as long as the procedures are followed.
NEW DEVELOPMENTS IN FIGHT AGAINST PROSTATE CANCER
Australian scientists say research on incurable prostrate cancer, to be released today, is a step along the way towards clinical trials in the battle against the cancer.
About two-and-a-half thousand Australian men die each year from prostate cancer, making it the second largest cause of cancer death among males.
Scientists from CSIRO and Sydney's Prince of Wales Hospital will today report on the research to an international conference on gene therapy at Thredbo in New South Wales.

CSIRO scientist Gerry Both says scientists have constructed a prototype virus with a toxin gene in it, that's been used to kill prostate cancer cells in a laboratory, and to reduce the size of tumours in mice.
CHARLEVILLE FLOODING MAY HAVE PEAKED
The Warrego river which has been flooding Charleville, in Queensland's southwest since the weekend is again beginning to drop.
Latest measurements put the river at 7.O metres and steady .
Power is cut to two thirds of Charleville while the Warrego Highway and Rail link to the town are now open.
BRITISH GOLF CHAMP PLAYS IN ADELAIDE
In golf...the favourite for this week's South Australian Open, British Open champion Tom Lehman (lay-man), will take part in the pro-am today, his first round on Adelaide's Kooyonga course.
The river reached 7.50 metres overnight, well below the level of the record 1990 flood.
The Charleville District Disaster Co-ordinator believes the worst of the flooding could be over.
There's been no further rain in Charleville or the Warrego catchment overnight.
No more homes have been evacuated .
781 people were forced to leave about 750 homes yesterday.
Last night the Red Cross and an Army Mobile Kitchen provided meals for 14-hundred people.
After arriving in Adelaide yesterday 37-year-old Lehman said his Christian beliefs had helped him overcome doubts about his career.
He also confirmed he'll will be without his regular caddy when he tees off in the tournament tomorrow.
Lehman's usual caddy, wife Melissa, is pregnant with the couple's fourth child.
MTIA URGES EMPLOYERS TO RESIST AGREEMENTS

The Metal Trades Industry Association says the Metal Trades Federation of Union's attempts to seal standard enterprise agreements has little regard for individual circumstances, and makes erroneous assumptions about economic conditions.
The MTIA warns the unions' 15 per cent wage claim ignores inflation predictions and threatens employment levels.
It's appealed to the two to three hundred employers facing enterprise bargaining in the next few months to resist more strongly the agreements.

It's been an on-going battle between the MTIA and the Unions over so-called pattern bargaining, or the Unions taking a standard enterprise agreement to all employers, aimed at ensuring standard outcomes for workers.
LITHIUM BATTERY EXPLODES AT MELBOURNE BARRACKS
In Melbourne overnight, six soldiers were hospitalised when a lithium battery used in a portable radio exploded and filled their barracks with fumes.
The Victorian Fire Brigade says the incident happened at the Simpson Army Barracks at Yallambe in Melbourne's northern suburbs, just after eleven last night.
A Fire Brigade spokesman says the soldiers, who were overcome by the fumes which were mildly toxic, were taken to hospital for observation but have since been released.
It's not known why the battery exploded.
